document.title: Agent 365 Security PoC
document.subtitle: Deployment procedures, control tests, and evidence requirements
document.description: Customer-facing definition of the Agent 365 Security PoC: what will be shown, how it is judged, and what runs live in the evaluation tenant.

purpose: This document is the customer-facing definition of the Agent 365 Security PoC: what will be shown, how it is judged, and what runs live in the evaluation tenant.
The full step-by-step procedures, scripts, and per-case test detail live in a separate reference pack and are cited by use-case ID.
The PoC runs entirely on trial licenses and trial service enablement. The agreed execution window is two weeks.
overview.control_plane: Agent 365 is an agent control plane. It integrates administration, identity, security, and compliance services. It does not replace hosting or orchestration.
overview.presentation_lead: This proof of concept tests Agent 365 controls against named test agents. It runs on trial licenses and trial service enablement in an agreed two-week window, with recorded positive and negative evidence for every live case.

modes.name: Live-proofed
modes.text: Executed in the evaluation tenant with recorded positive and negative evidence, following the acceptance rules in the scope document.

modes.name: Demonstration only
modes.text: Presented by the delivery team as a guided walkthrough or in a separate demonstration environment. These items were moved out of live proofing due to time constraints. They are not product limitations unless explicitly recorded as a coverage gap.

overview.deferred_required: Where the original test catalogue marked a demonstration-only case as required (ONB-03, ONB-05, ONB-07, ONB-10), acceptance for this two-week PoC is assessed against the live-proofed set. The deferred cases are shown as demonstrations and can be scheduled as a follow-up phase.
overview.reference_pack: Detailed procedures are maintained as guides (deployment and configuration, numbered in execution order) and test procedures (one per test case). The delivery team executes from the reference pack; the scope document is the contract for scope and acceptance.

environment: A dedicated evaluation tenant with trial licensing, named test users (u-allow, u-deny), test groups, and a dedicated Power Platform environment.
One onboarded Windows test device with Defender for Endpoint Plan 2, active Antivirus, and real-time protection, for local-agent discovery.

Synthetic fixtures only: public-procedure and restricted-record test files carrying the markers POC-APPROVAL-6142 and POC-RESTRICTED-4826. No customer data, production connectors, or production credentials at any point.

An optional isolated Azure lab (dedicated resource group, Log Analytics workspace, Application Insights, optional Sentinel onboarding and Azure OpenAI deployment), created only after explicit approval and removed by the guarded cleanup scripts at the end.
stop_conditions: A test would touch a production identity, device, resource, or agent.
An agent reads real restricted data.
Policy scope differs from the approved scope.
A required licence, consent, or feature is absent.
The approved usage limit or end time is reached.

required_demonstrations.proof: Registration, identity, authenticated use, and supported controls.
Hosting, publication, identity, and explicit Agent 365 telemetry.
Deployment, provider authorization, and actual interaction evidence.
Model execution, explicit instrumentation, and service-side telemetry.
Provider inventory synchronization and supported management actions.
Preview workspace connection and inventory synchronization.
Record the unsupported connector request. Use a separate SDK demonstration.
Local discovery and separately configured endpoint controls.

rules: Run both the positive phase and the negative phase for each case.
Record the actual service decision and the actual action result.
Keep policy mode, scope, identity, timestamps, and correlation evidence.
Report required and optional cases separately.
Report approved exclusions with their original and revised denominators.
Keep local simulation results separate from live product results.
Keep a blocked case in the original denominator.
cautions: A screenshot of a configured policy does not prove enforcement.
A model refusal does not prove that a security service blocked the request.
An empty query result does not prove that the agent performed no action.
evidence: Every live case runs a positive and a negative phase, records the actual service decision and action result, and is reviewed against its pass criteria.
Results use PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT_RUN. A blocked case stays in the original denominator and is never re-labelled to pass.

Evidence is captured with the kit's local evidence recorder into a protected store outside the repository: UTC times, policy mode and scope, identities, correlation IDs, and artifact hashes for both phases of every case.
The final review issues the customer result with the agreed scope, product versions and preview states, the acceptance report, and every coverage gap listed explicitly.
acceptance.demonstrations: Demonstration-only items are recorded as demonstrations with date, audience, and what was shown. They do not enter the live acceptance denominator.

cleanup: At the end of the window: contain and retire the test agents, restore every changed policy to its recorded value, revoke test consents and provider credentials, remove test deployments, and remove the optional Azure lab through the guarded exact-ID removal plan (the resource group and deployment history are retained). Residual objects that cannot be deleted through supported interfaces are recorded with an owner rather than claimed removed.

live_areas.title: Copilot Studio agent
live_areas.summary: Create, register, and publish an authenticated Studio agent with synthetic knowledge. Verify draft and published registry identity, scoped audience deployment, and the authenticated-channel boundary.

live_areas.title: Foundry hosted agent with explicit telemetry
live_areas.summary: Deploy the bounded hosted sample in two phases: export off, then a single narrow observability grant (Agent365.Observability.OtelWrite) and export on. Prove publication, registry identity, one authorized synthetic invocation with a correlated Agent 365 trace, and the negative export-disabled run.

live_areas.title: SDK-enabled custom agent
live_areas.summary: Run the outbound-only Python harness against an approved Azure OpenAI deployment: blueprint and child Agent ID provisioning, registration-only CLI, explicit metadata-only export, and the negative permission test. This is the deepest identity chain in the PoC and anchors the Entra demonstrations.

live_areas.title: Local agents: Codex CLI, Claude Code, OpenClaw
live_areas.summary: Install supported local agents on the test device, run harmless synthetic sessions, and verify Defender local-agent discovery (user, device, agent type, configured MCP metadata) plus the AgentsInfo hunting query. Discovery only; runtime blocking previews are demonstration-only.

live_areas.title: OpenAI connector boundary
live_areas.summary: Record, against the live provider selector, that no native OpenAI Connected platforms connector exists as of the verification date, and show the supported alternative (the SDK-enabled path). This is a documented coverage gap, not a failed test.

live_areas.title: Microsoft 365 governance and lifecycle
live_areas.summary: Registry review, scoped distribution to the approved test group, reader-versus-administrator boundary, Foundry admin Block versus compute Stop, and retirement of an owned agent.

live_areas.title: Entra Agent ID and Conditional Access
live_areas.summary: Map agent identities and permissions. Prove delegated (on-behalf-of) policy against the user, autonomous policy against the agent identity, least-privilege consent, identity disablement with measured token persistence, and the API-key boundary that Conditional Access cannot govern.

live_areas.title: Defender security for AI
live_areas.summary: Connect Security for AI with the Microsoft 365 connector, verify agent inventory and posture for the live test agents, and distinguish assessed indicators from Not evaluated. Runtime audit/block fixtures are demonstration-only.

live_areas.title: Defender for Endpoint
live_areas.summary: Local-agent discovery evidence on the onboarded device, including the configured-MCP-versus-executed-tool boundary.

live_areas.title: Defender for Cloud and Defender for Cloud Apps
live_areas.summary: Separate cloud AI infrastructure posture from agent-level coverage on the lab subscription (DFC-01). Discover and block one unsanctioned test AI domain for the test device group and review OAuth app governance (MDCA-01, MDCA-02).

live_areas.title: Purview
live_areas.summary: Classify the synthetic restricted marker (PUR-04), prove Studio Word/PowerPoint label inheritance (PUR-05), restrict Studio SharePoint grounding with label-based DLP (PUR-06), and find the interaction in Purview Audit (PUR-10). Retention and eDiscovery verification (PUR-11, PUR-12) start live but their wait periods can complete after the window; instance-level DLP is demonstration-only.

live_areas.title: Sentinel
live_areas.summary: Connect Agent 365 lake telemetry, Defender XDR incidents, and Entra sign-in/audit logs. Correlate the SDK agent's synthetic session in the lake and verify connector independence.

live_areas.title: Security Copilot
live_areas.summary: Analyst verification workflow over one real PoC incident: summary fidelity, hunting-query validation against real schemas, and authorization boundaries.

live_areas.title: Response and cleanup
live_areas.summary: Contain the test agent on every mapped execution path, restore service without restoring prohibited access, and reconstruct the incident timeline separating configuration, decision, execution, and side effect.

demo_items.title: Partner SaaS agent, Zendesk
demo_items.reason: Depends on partner licensing and a vendor test workspace that cannot be provisioned inside the window.

demo_items.title: Amazon Bedrock provider lab and Connected platforms sync
demo_items.reason: Requires an eligible AWS account (Agents Classic closed to new customers), approved connector credentials including deletion authority, and the preview sync rollout.

demo_items.title: Anthropic Claude Managed Agents sync
demo_items.reason: Provider APIs are beta and the Microsoft connection is preview; approval lead times exceed the window.

demo_items.title: Frontier and Foundry autopilot pathway
demo_items.reason: Preview enrollment, seat management, and sample drift gates.

demo_items.title: BYO MCP server approval and blocking
demo_items.reason: Preview with a currently undeletable registration; shown as a walkthrough.

demo_items.title: Defender runtime protection previews
demo_items.reason: Audit/block fixtures on Foundry, Studio, and local agents require preview features and customer-approved detector fixtures; shown live in a demonstration environment instead.

demo_items.title: OpenClaw whole-application blocking
demo_items.reason: Documented propagation is 15 minutes to eight hours and the action can affect all Intune-managed Windows devices; it is only safe in a disposable tenant.

demo_items.title: Purview instance-level protections
demo_items.reason: Depend on eligible Agent 365 instances, Frontier mailboxes, and retention processing periods.

demo_items.title: Global Secure Access network and prompt controls
demo_items.reason: Require TLS-inspection certificate deployment and routed-client setup on managed devices.

demo_items.title: Sentinel agent-identities preview connector
demo_items.reason: Preview connector. Deferred to a demonstration because of the two-week time constraint.

extra_guides.title: PoC close-out: acceptance review and customer result
extra_guides.origin: Scope document revision 1.1: Evidence and acceptance, Demonstration-only scope, and Cleanup.
paragraphs: This guide closes the two-week PoC. It applies the evidence, demonstration, and cleanup rules from the customer scope document.
Complete it on Days 13-14, after every dependent case and the final cleanup in guides 43 and 44.

sections.title: Review live acceptance with the customer
steps: Confirm every live-proofed case has recorded positive and negative phases with evidence.
Run the evidence verify and report commands against the protected evidence store.
Review each live case against its pass criteria with the evidence reviewer.
Keep blocked cases in the original denominator. Record each reason and owner.
Record approved exclusions with their original and revised denominators.
notes: Results use PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, or NOT_RUN. A blocked case is never re-labelled to pass.
A screenshot of a configured policy does not prove enforcement.

sections.title: Record demonstration-only items
steps: Record each demonstration with its date, audience, environment, and what was shown.
Keep demonstrations outside the live acceptance denominator.
Record customer interest in a follow-up live phase for each deferred item.
notes: Deferrals are time decisions. Record a product limitation only as an explicit coverage gap.

sections.title: Issue the customer result
steps: State the agreed scope, product versions, and preview states used during execution.
Attach the acceptance report. List every coverage gap explicitly.
Confirm cleanup completion. Record residual objects with an owner rather than claiming removal.
Share the final report and approved notes with the customer sponsor.
notes: Share only notes marked for the customer. Keep internal notes and raw evidence in the protected store.
